program.name: ndm_slicebinary
program.help:
Copy a subset of channels out of a session binary into its own smaller binary.
Reads <session>.<inputExtension> and writes <session>.<inputExtension>.slice.<tag> containing only the listed channels, in the order listed. The source file is opened read-only and is never modified, so slicing is always safe to re-run.
The output extension mirrors the input rather than being fixed to lfp. A slice of the wide-band .dat is still wide-band data, and calling it .lfp.slice.<tag> would tell every downstream consumer it had been decimated when it had not. So slicing the lfp gives .lfp.slice.<tag> and slicing the dat gives .dat.slice.<tag>.
Channel count and sample width come from the session's acquisitionSystem block (nChannels, nBits), so the slice cannot disagree with the recording it came from. The engine refuses a file whose length is not a whole number of records, which catches a wrong channel count or sample width -- but only when the mismatch leaves a remainder, so it is a safety net and not a guarantee.
Alongside the binary, a plain-text <output>.info records the five numbers a reader needs to parse the file and map it back: the SOURCE channel count, the sample width, the channel list, the input extension and the sampling rate of the stream that was cut. nChannels and nBits together fix the byte layout -- without both, the file cannot be indexed, and a wrong guess yields a file of the right length full of wrong numbers. Nothing derivable is duplicated there: channel grouping, anatomy and spike geometry are all functions of slicedChannels against the parent session, and a copy would be the one that goes stale when the parent is regrouped.
Running again with the same tag is refused because the output already exists; pick a different tag or remove the file.
PARAMETERS
# slicedChannels
Channels to copy, 0-based, in the order they should appear in the output. Comma- or whitespace-separated (0,1,4 and 0 1 4 are equivalent). Order is preserved, so the list can also reorder channels, and a channel may be repeated to duplicate it. Leaving this empty means "no slice requested": the stage reports that and succeeds, so an unconfigured node does not fail a whole pipeline run.
Only plain integers are accepted. Unlike process_extractchannels, the gain (5*1.5) and post-hoc reference (5-2) spellings are refused rather than honoured, because a slice is meant to be a byte-exact excerpt and a stray character silently yielding a derived signal is invisible downstream.
# tag
Names the output: <session>.<inputExtension>.slice.<tag>. Letters, digits, - and _ only; a tag containing a dot, a slash or whitespace is refused, since it is a filename component rather than a path.
# inputExtension
Data file to slice, without the leading dot (default lfp). Point it at the wide-band recording (dat), the filtered signal (fil), or any other externally-processed source to excerpt that instead.
